sections.overview: This sphinx moth occurs from the southwestern United States into Mexico.
sections.identification: Its dark-grey forewings have wavy black and pale-grey lines; its black hindwings have two pale bands.
sections.habitat: The species account reports no habitat.
sections.diet: Larval host records are uncertain: one species account lists tomato only as a possibility, whereas a 2025 North American host-plant checklist records *Salvia* and explicitly does not list tomato.
sections.behavior: It probably has one brood, from late June to early August.
sections.reproduction: The fully grown caterpillar pupates in an underground burrow, where it overwinters.
sections.ecology: Adult nectar-feeding is only suggested, not confirmed.
sections.conservation: Its G4 rank is apparently secure, but it may be locally rare near the range edge.
